## Identity-aware Execution (IAE)

Govern external Worker actions through explicit identities, managed Connections, versioned authorization policies, obligations, durable pre-effect decisions and attributable audit evidence; provider enforcement is verified per execution mode, never assumed.

## Operations History at Scale (OHS)

Keep instance replay intelligible and responsive with grouped multi-instance execution, bounded iteration discovery and exact causal drill-down at 50,000 iterations.

**[Programme plan](../planning/operations-history-at-scale-program.md) · [Roadmap track](../../ROADMAP.md#milestone-4--operability-) · [Manifest](ohs/program.json) · Reviewed: 2026-11-02**

| **OHS1** — Default grouped multi-instance history | complete | pblumer | — | [PR #1483](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1483), [Issue #1481](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/issues/1481) | PR #1483 merged: grouped history is available in Operations, while legacy timeline loading remains unbounded until OHS2/OHS3.; [Evidence 1](../planning/operations-history-at-scale-program.md) |
| **OHS2** — Bounded iteration lookup and filtering | active | pblumer | OHS1 | [PR #1487](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1487), [PR #1488](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1488), [PR #1490](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1490), [PR #1496](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1496), [PR #1502](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1502), [PR #1507](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1507), [PR #1513](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1513), [Issue #1481](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/issues/1481), [Issue #1494](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/issues/1494) | #1487 (keys), #1488 (projection), #1490 (fail-closed readiness) #1496 (index v2, bounded API, 50k acceptance) and #1502 (Multi-Instance Explorer, startup rebuild of older stores) merged. Index schema v2 adds loopCounter order, lifecycle-state and incident families, write-only body counters and nested-body parents; api/mihistory serves the cursor-paged, off-writer, HMAC-cursor API and MCP tools with a 50,000-iteration end-to-end acceptance. The Operations Multi-Instance Explorer and a timeline-free view for large instances are built (e2e/mi-explorer.spec.mjs). The instance outline (cfOutline, instance_outline_v1) gives the bounded view the instance's own steps (#1507, merged). Open: per-instance readiness for compacted logs, and the HTTP-level 50k acceptance for an MI subprocess; #1494 (quadratic MI-subprocess completion) is fixed by a per-scope trigger index (#1513, merged). Stores that predate the index are rebuilt at startup from the retained log (accepted shadow-replay ADR draft).; [Evidence 1](../../api/mihistory/acceptance_test.go), [Evidence 2](../../engine/miindex_v2_recovery_test.go), [Evidence 3](../adr/0517-scalable-instance-replay.md), [Evidence 4](../../e2e/mi-explorer.spec.mjs), [Evidence 5](../../engine/mirebuild_test.go) |
| **OHS3** — Scalable iteration detail replay | active | pblumer | OHS2 | [PR #1502](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1502), [PR #1508](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1508), [PR #1514](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/pull/1514), [Issue #1481](https://github.com/pblumer/atlas/issues/1481) | Increment 1 (#1502, merged): one iteration's recorded scope variables and its attributed DMN decisions (cfMIDecision, own readiness marker), in the API and the explorer. Increment 2 (#1508, merged): the replay window of one iteration — the steps inside it (cfIterationStep, readiness marker mi_iteration_steps_v1, covered by the startup rebuild), a bounded route and MCP tool, and a step-by-step replay on the diagram in the explorer; 1,110 bytes / 1.2 ms for iteration 37,421 of the 50k acceptance instance. Increment 3 (#1514, in review): the variables of the iteration's own scopes as they stood at each step (bounded fold of the existing per-scope snapshot history; 519 bytes / 0.9 ms at 50k), in the API, MCP and under the replay window. Open: the body's and the instance's variables at a step, collapsed-subprocess planes, job/user-task history per iteration, and the retention/migration verification.; [Evidence 1](../../engine/miindex_v2_recovery_test.go), [Evidence 2](../../api/mihistory/service_test.go), [Evidence 3](../../state/outline_test.go), [Evidence 4](../../api/mihistory/acceptance_test.go), [Evidence 5](../../e2e/mi-explorer.spec.mjs) |

## Worker Type Distribution (WTD)

Worker Types become signed artifacts that atlas installs, verifies and launches and atlas hub distributes, for atlas, commercial, third-party and organisation-internal publishers; the server half becomes data, and the built-in Worker Types are migrated, not grandfathered (ADR-0535).

**[Programme plan](../adr/0535-worker-types-as-distributed-artifacts.md) · [Roadmap track](../../ROADMAP.md#milestone-6--ecosystem-) · [Manifest](wtd/program.json) · Reviewed: 2026-11-09**

Open gate: owner acceptance; no approving review is recorded on the PRs, so the slice is not set complete.
